text:
Priya A.: Quick heads-up: Sofia accepted offer (Sr Data Engineer) and is scheduled to start 2026-04-01. Portugal payroll cutoff is 2026-03-29 so her first regular pay won't land until 4/30. Requesting approval for: (1) one-time onboarding advance = 50% of monthly base, payable within first payroll window; (2) temporary comp-band uplift of +1 band for 90 days while relocation and market alignment are finalized. Need routing for comp committee and payroll tax guidance. @Ruth (People Ops) @Leo

Evan G.: Can we do advance as 50% immediate + 50% on first full payroll? Also confirm whether this should be an amendment to the offer or processed separately as onboarding expense.

Priya A.: Prefer advance instead of sign-on to avoid complex deferred bonus language. If approved, we'll update offer to include the advance and clawback clause.

Ruth (People Ops): Initial flags: - Cross-border advances can affect withholding and benefits deductions. - Temporary uplift needs exec sponsor and a scheduled review at 30 days to confirm ongoing band. - Do we want a clawback if the new hire leaves within the probation period? Recommend: "repayable if employment terminates within 90 days."

Leo (Hiring Manager): I sponsor the uplift. Hiring team ok with 90-day clawback. We can commit to regular check-ins.

Evan G.: @PeopleOpsBot please run payroll impact calc for Portugal for 50% monthly advance and show estimated withholding, employer cost delta, and suggested gross-up options.

PeopleOpsBot: payroll-impact-calc started: country=PT amount=0.5*monthly_base. Est employee withholding diff = ~4.2% of gross advance; est net advance ~46% of monthly_base after statutory deductions. Employer social contributions unaffected in standard advance flow. See internal doc: /docs/payroll/pt-advances.md

Finance (Payroll): FYI from payroll: we can process advance in first payroll cycle but it will be subject to local withholding. If you want net protected (gross-up), we need comp committee approval for gross-up amount and tax handling. Processing as a separate expense vs. amendment: payroll prefers separate one-off payment to avoid reissuing the offer, but People Ops prefers offer amendment for legal clarity.

Ruth (People Ops): Decision points for routing: 1) Approve 50% onboarding advance payable within first payroll window (yes/no). 2) Approve temporary +1 comp band for 90 days with automatic revert and 30-day manager review (yes/no). 3) Clawback: "advance repayable if employment terminates within 90 days" confirmed? 4) Gross-up: do we gross-up to protect net?

Priya A.: Confirm clawback language as above. No gross-up requested unless comp committee pushes. We prefer the advance to be processed as a one-off payroll payment but will accept offer amendment if legal requires.

Evan G.: I'm assembling the comp packet (candidate comps, market rationale, payroll calc, proposed clawback text). ETA ~2 hours, routing to comp-committee+finance after prep.

Ruth (People Ops): Routing now to comp-committee. Please review and vote. If approved by comp committee + finance, People Ops will update offer and notify payroll to process the payment. I'll track decision in GDrive: /hr/onboarding-exceptions/2026/sofia-pt-onboard-advance.docx

Leo (Hiring Manager): Appreciate the quick handling. Candidate is okay with start date but we need the advance to avoid losing them. :rocket:

Priya A.: Standing by for committee reply and updated offer text. If approved, I'll send amended offer tonight with the clause: "Onboarding advance equal to 50% of one months base salary payable within the first payroll window; repayable in full if employment terminates within 90 days."

PeopleOpsBot: comp-packet generated and uploaded: /internal/comp-review/3387654321/packet.pdf

Ruth (People Ops): thanks everyone. Will post committee decision in thread once received.

Leo (Hiring Manager): thanks team :thumbsup:
